findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The `totpStep1` key previously held a Lithuanian translation (`Įdiekite <a href="https://freeotp.github.io/"...`) that was replaced with Italian text (`Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`). The neighboring keys `totpStep2` and `totpStep3` remain in Lithuanian, so the file becomes internally inconsistent. This is a translation regression: the original Lithuanian content is lost and a wrong-language string is now displayed to Lithuanian users. The new HTML sanitizer cannot catch this since it only validates HTML safety, not language correctness.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The `loginTotpStep1` key previously held a Lithuanian translation (`Įdiekite <a href="https://freeotp.github.io/"...`) and was replaced with the Italian string `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Surrounding `loginTotpStep2` and `loginTotpStep3` are still Lithuanian, making the file internally inconsistent. The Lithuanian translation is now lost to users. The new sanitizer does not verify language matches and therefore will not detect this regression.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese translation replaced with Traditional Chinese
findings.body: The `totpStep1` key in this Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN) was changed from Simplified Chinese text (`在你的设备上安装 ... Google Authenticator.两个应用可以从 ...`) to Traditional Chinese text (`在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`). Characters like `您`, `手機`, `安裝`, `程式` are Traditional; the file should use Simplified forms. zh_CN users will now see Traditional Chinese on this screen, breaking locale expectations.

findings.title: English source `templateHelp` typo `<NAME >` not fixed
findings.body: The English source string `templateHelp` contains `CLAIM.<NAME > ...` with a stray trailing space inside the angle brackets (`<NAME >` instead of `<NAME>`). The Chinese translation in `messages_zh_CN.properties` was corrected to `CLAIM.<NAME>`, but the English source on which all other translations are based still contains the typo. Any future translation that copies the English literally will reintroduce the typo. The verifier handles this for `templateHelp` via `normalizeValue`, but only for that specific key; the underlying source string is inconsistent with the rest of the translations.

findings.title: HTML_TAGS regex is too restrictive for HTML detection
findings.body: `HTML_TAGS` is defined as `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`. This only matches tags whose first character after `<` is a lowercase ASCII letter, so `<DIV>`, `<H1>`, `<h1>`, `<a1>` and any tag name containing a digit or uppercase letter will not be detected. The OWASP sanitizer is case-insensitive and HTML spec tags are case-insensitive, so this leads to false negatives in `containsHtml()` and inconsistent classification between POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML. In practice this can produce false positives (e.g. English `<H1>` falls through to POLICY_NO_HTML, the sanitizer strips the tag, and the verifier reports `Illegal HTML` for the translation even though both sides are identical). Fix by using a case-insensitive pattern or by parsing via the sanitizer itself.

findings.title: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException, not MojoExecutionException
findings.body: `verifySafeHtml()` is called from `verify()` which declares `throws MojoExecutionException`. However `verifySafeHtml()` catches `IOException` and rethrows it as `new RuntimeException(...)`. A `RuntimeException` is not caught by the surrounding `catch (IOException e)` block in `verify()`, so it propagates unchecked and aborts the build with an unhandled exception instead of being wrapped into a `MojoExecutionException` with the existing error formatting. Either rethrow as `MojoExecutionException` (and declare it) or add the message to the `messages` list so the build produces a useful diagnostic.

findings.title: Method name `santizeAnchors` is misspelled
findings.body: `santizeAnchors` should be spelled `sanitizeAnchors`. This is a public-facing method name (well, package-private, but reachable as a Java identifier in the codebase), so the typo propagates to anyone reading or extending the code.

findings.title: Limited test coverage of HTML sanitizer behavior
findings.body: The added tests cover only the simplest cases: duplicate keys, illegal HTML tag, HTML where the English has none, and changed anchor URL. They do not cover: (1) the legitimate-translation case where English has HTML and target has the same HTML (which should pass); (2) case-insensitive HTML in the English source; (3) HTML-like placeholders such as `<NAME>` or `<USERNAME>` in messages that are not whitelisted in `normalizeValue`; (4) multiple anchors; (5) anchors that differ only in inner text but keep the same URL (legitimate translations of link text); (6) `errorTitleHtml`-style keys where the English contains `<strong>` and the translation must keep it. Adding these tests would catch regressions in the sanitizer logic and the normalization rules.

findings.title: normalizeValue special-cases only a few keys, risking false positives
findings.body: `normalizeValue` strips HTML-looking content only for `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, and `error-invalid-multivalued-size`. Any other message that legitimately contains text resembling an HTML tag (e.g., `<NAME>`, `<USERNAME>`, `<EMAIL>`, or any other MessageFormat placeholder that the translator chose to write with angle brackets) will be stripped by the OWASP sanitizer under POLICY_NO_HTML and the verifier will incorrectly report `Illegal HTML`. For example, any key like `fooBarTemplate=Hello <NAME>` will fail verification because `<NAME>` is not an allowed tag. Either broaden the placeholder normalization or detect via the sanitizer whether the English contains any disallowed HTML before applying POLICY_NO_HTML (i.e., compare normalized values against sanitized English, not against the raw translation).
